subject: Trading
title: John Paulson: The Greatest Trade Ever
description: Learn John Paulson: The Greatest Trade Ever in one minute.

hook.text: John Paulson made $15 billion shorting subprime mortgages in 2007-2008. The largest single trade profit in history.

buildup.text: Paulson was a merger arbitrage specialist—not a macro trader—who pivoted when he spotted the housing bubble.

discovery.text: He hired a team to analyze every subprime mortgage pool. They found bonds rated AAA that were certain to fail.

twist.text: After his triumph, Paulson made terrible bets—gold, pharma, Puerto Rico—losing billions over the next decade.

climax.text: One legendary trade doesn't make a legendary career. Paulson's story shows both the peak and the peril of conviction.

punchline.text: The greatest trade ever was followed by some of the worst.

quiz.question: What happened to Paulson's performance after his legendary 2008 trade?
options: He lost billions on subsequent bets in gold, pharma, and Puerto Rico
